title: N-able says attackers accessed a Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud server
date_note: N-able began investigating a disruption on 16 Nov; the security incident was disclosed on Wednesday 18 Nov per The Hacker News, which gives no exact disclosure date.
summary: N-able says unknown actors accessed one server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud, and it found no evidence customer data was compromised. N-able told SecurityWeek exploitation was confined to a single hosted server and the impacted functionality is restored. Per The Hacker News, a separate SSRF flaw, CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS 4.0 score 9.3), was found during the investigation; N-able has not said whether it was the way in.
plain: A security vendor's email filtering service was breached on one server. N-able told SecurityWeek the affected functionality is restored.
exec: N-able told SecurityWeek the email filtering service's impacted functionality is restored and exploitation was confined to one hosted server.
action: As The Hacker News reports N-able's advisory, SpamExperts Local Cloud operators should confirm they run build 20261121.1943; Hosted Cloud users have nothing to install. N-able told SecurityWeek it revoked customer API tokens and reset local-user passwords.
impact: Portal and API access were disabled during the incident (SecurityWeek, 20 Nov); N-able told SecurityWeek on 23 Nov it has restored the impacted functionality.

evidence.quote: The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-134624, is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw.
The advisory gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.3

validation.note: The Hacker News relays N-able's own statement; N-able's status page (uptime.n-able.com/event/202672) returned 403 to our reader, so it was not read. GBHackers (19 Nov) relays the same N-able notice: more detail, not independent confirmation. 20 Nov: SecurityWeek (N-able's own statement to the outlet, status page cited) adds possible credential access and containment steps; same N-able notice, not independent confirmation.

review.note: source published days added; action advice attributed to The Hacker News and SecurityWeek, not N-able directly
